notes: Version 1.18. O19 1.3 leaves its independence tests open and withdraws its pipeline-independence proposition (now Open Problem 7.2), so O20 uses the O19 canonical pair observable as a proposed, case-dependent observable, not as a constructed convention-free one; the uniqueness and invariance statements built on it are withdrawn as results. The values r(c,q) in {1,2,3,4} are a historical hypothesis; O16 shows r = 1 on the real pipeline within its contract, and O17's normalisation statement is internal to its toy model. Section 2.2 no longer attributes to O16 a machine-precision verification, the value 7.44 or variance and R^2 figures: O16 proves the doubling only if the ratio is shell-independent and asserts no numerical exponent. The power-law regime is an input for the uncorrected pair observable. The persistence template and its conditional threshold-crossing algebra are unchanged.
